deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is an oscillation (period) determination for Gauss's absolute measurement of the horizontal intensity of the Earth's magnetic field (Intensitas vis magneticae, 1832–33). Needle/bar no. 31 is loaded with weights at two settings ('Belastet mit 1000 …, 0 — 700'). The next page has the companion settings 250 — 450 and a repeat of 0 — 700. The difference of the squared periods between the two weight settings yields the moment of inertia, and hence the product M·T.

(1) Transit times. For selected oscillation numbers n, the clock time t_n of a transit is recorded: n = 0–3, 14–19, 24–27, 62–67 and 84–87. The run starts at 11h39m02.75s and ends after midnight at 0h30m50.00s.

(2) Reduction with an assumed period. Each time is reduced with the trial period T0 = 35.72 s ('Reducirt mit 35"72'):
 r_n = t_n − n·T0, written as seconds after 11h39m.
If the period were exactly 35.72 s, r_n would be constant. Any linear drift in r_n gives the correction to T0. Gauss's reduced values are:
- n = 0–3: 2.75, 2.48, 2.71, 3.15
- n = 14–19: 3.67, 3.25, 3.38, 3.31, 3.29, 3.02
- n = 24–27: 3.17, 3.30, 3.13, 3.01
- n = 62–67: 2.51, 2.49, 2.47, 2.45, 2.43, 2.56
- n = 84–87: 2.42, 2.50, 2.43, 2.36
The scatter is unusually large; group 14–19 jumps by about 0.9 s from n = 0–3.

(3) Scale readings. Beside n = 1, 2, 64, 85 and 86 are pairs of the form (rest point, arc of swing) in scale divisions:
- n = 1: 586.95, 508.1
- n = 2: 586.775, 504.15
- n = 64: 583.525, 327.55
- n = 85: 584.35, 299.1
- n = 86: 584.75, 296.9

(4) Logarithmic decrement. 'Decr. log. 0.00275' is the Briggsian log decrement per oscillation, λ = [log10 A_m − log10 A_n]/(n − m).
- My check, end amplitudes: log10(508.1/296.9)/85 = 0.23334/85 = 0.002745 ≈ 0.00275.
- Using the mean amplitudes at n = 1.5 and 85.5 instead gives 0.00274.
- The decrement is not uniform: about 0.0030 between n ≈ 1.5 and 64, and about 0.0019 between 64 and 85.5.

(5) Verdict and period. Gauss rejects the series ('Diese Reihe wird verworfen, weil die ersten Messungen fehlerhaft sind'). He nevertheless records the period from the most probable combination: 1 oscillation = 35.71143 s, i.e. a correction of −0.00857 s to T0. The note 'ohne Red. auf unendl. kl. B[ögen]' says this period is not yet reduced to infinitely small arcs.

My reconstruction of the period:
- An ordinary least-squares line r = a + b·n through all 24 reduced values gives b = −203.90/21992 = −0.00927, so T = 35.7107 s. This is close to, but not identical with, 35.71143.
- Comparing the group means of n = 14–27 with n = 62–87 gives T ≈ 35.7050.
- Comparing the first three groups with the last two gives T ≈ 35.7088.
Gauss's exact weighting ('Combination') cannot be recovered with certainty. His figure lies within the spread of these reasonable combinations, consistent with the instability that led him to reject the series.
errors: n = 3: 11h40m50.30s − 3·35.72 s gives 3.14, but 3.15 is written. This is a trivial rounding or reading slip of 0.01 s.
All other reduced values check exactly against t_n − n·35.72.

The final period 35.71143 s cannot be reproduced exactly by a plain least-squares fit (35.7107) or by simple group-mean comparisons (35.705–35.709). Gauss's weighting is not stated. The series is anyway declared defective by Gauss himself, so this is not an error in the sense of a wrong step.
The log decrement 0.00275 is consistent with the end amplitudes (0.002745), but the damping is visibly non-uniform across the run. This is another sign of the faulty series.

results.what: Determination of the oscillation period by reducing transit times with a trial period and fitting the linear drift of the residuals (most probable value)
results.modern_name: Linear least-squares estimation of period from timed transits (residual/O−C method)
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss (least squares, 1809; applied in Intensitas vis magneticae 1832)

results.what: Logarithmic decrement of the swing amplitude from scale readings
results.modern_name: Logarithmic decrement of a damped oscillator
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and Weber, magnetometer practice of the 1830s

results.what: Period measurement with added weights at two positions, to obtain the moment of inertia for absolute intensity
results.modern_name: Gauss's method for absolute measurement of horizontal geomagnetic intensity (moment-of-inertia part)

results.what: Mention of reduction of the period to infinitely small arcs (not applied here)
results.usually_credited_to: Standard 18th-century pendulum theory; used by Gauss

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine laboratory record of Gauss's 1833 absolute-intensity measurements, using the reduction method, log decrement and loaded-bar technique he published in Intensitas vis magneticae. The only point of interest is the documentary detail of a rejected series and his period estimate for it.

checkable.asserts: Reduced value for n=3 is 3.14 (Gauss wrote 3.15)
Reduced value for n=62 (0h15m57.15 = 12h15m57.15 after the 11h start) is 2.51
Log decrement per oscillation ≈ 0.002745, matching Decr. log. 0.00275
Plain least-squares period over all 24 reduced values ≈ 35.7107 s, close to Gauss's 35.71143

transcription_corrections: n=1: the time reads 38.20 (a '2' corrected/overwritten) and the reduced value is 2.48. Arithmetic confirms 39m38.20s − 35.72s = 39m02.48s.
Gloss on the last line: 'ohne Red. auf unendl. kl. B.' means 'ohne Reduction auf unendlich kleine Bögen' (no reduction to infinitely small arcs).
'Confection[?]' is uncertain; the sense requires something like 'Combination' (most probable combination).
Marginal labels 'Sat.' and 'Jch' are uncertain readings of marginal annotations; they are not part of the numeric data.
'Decr. log.' (decrementum logarithmicum) is correct as transcribed.
